newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba denies Tietmeyer denied agreement with Bonn.
newsitem.headline: Buba denies Tietmeyer denied agreement with Bonn.

text.p: The Bundesbank on Wednesday denied reports that Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, speaking in Interlaken, Switzerland, had denied there was an agreement in talks with Bonn on revaluation of Bundesbank assets.
The central bank made clear that, as originally reported by Reuters, Tietmeyer had said that a formal deal had not yet been completed but that the two sides were close to an agreement.
Some reports had interpreted Tietmeyer's comments as denying that there had been an agreement.
A statement, read out to news agencies by a Bundesbank spokesman in a telephone conference, said:

"The reports that the Bundesbank President denied the outcome of the talks are wrong. The Bundesbank President and Finance Minister Theo Waigel made clear that no formal agreement has been reached. The appropriate bodies have yet to give their approval."

Tietmeyer and Waigel met for talks yesterday to seek a solution to a dispute between the government and the Bundesbank over plans to raise the value of Bundesbank assets to a value closer to market prices.

The Bundesbank had objected to plans to transfer the funds raised to Bonn this year, the key year for qualification for a single currency, on the grounds that this could distort the Maastricht Treaty entry test.
